reader: Claude Opus 5.5, research reader with the source at hand
reason: The first reading was not blind (its reader saw the typed slip first) and left abraded names and lines unresolved; rereading with AH at hand resolved the strophe text, e.g. 'decus' for 'deus', 'quam transitoria' for 'historia', and the Adl. piece's 'Perit enim rerum maneries'.
sources: G. M. Dreves (ed.), Analecta Hymnica 49 (Leipzig, 1906), no. 779, 'Super Libera me Domine', pp. 378-380 (archive.org hymniineditilitu49drev, page images n381-n383)
Cantus 003732, Media vita in morte sumus (offset only)
text:
F-ag0c (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 7) - SOURCE-ASSISTED READING, not a blind reading. Made with Analecta Hymnica 49 no. 779 available; the typed slip photographed with the pieces (canvases 4-6) was also seen. Lines reread on the image: both text blocks of Frg. 7-11v (6 lines each), the pasted Adl. piece (5 lines), the mirrored and contrast-stretched offset on 7-8v (6 lines), and fragments of the mirrored offset on 7-10v. Base: readings/stams-2026-10-30-image-only.json (itself not blind: its reader saw the slip first). Documentary notes not read; notation not transcribed.
Boxes are native pixels x1,y1-x2,y2 on 7360 x 4912 images. [abc] = lost or supplied; ? = uncertain; (abc) = expansion.

IDENTIFIED TEXT: Audi tellus (AH 49 no. 779), strophes 1-6

Canvas 5 (Stams_STA_Frg_007_09v11v_Adl_01v_1_), 2600,250-3750,2150, 7-11v right block:
1 [A]udi tellus audi ma[gni maris]
2 [li]mbus. Audi omne [quod vivit sub]
3 [sole] huius mundi decus et [gloria]
4 sunt falsa q(uam) transitoria Con[testantur]
5 temporalia non in uno statu [manentia]
6 N[ichil] enim Regalis dign[itas]

Canvas 6 (Stams_STA_Frg_007_09v11v_Adl_01v_2_), 3450,2750-5000,4850, rotated 180 degrees, Adl. piece (line 5 on the strip beneath it):
1 [aur]i congeries Perit enim rerum
2 maneries et transit rerum materies [ut]
3 liquescet a sole glacies Ubi fortes
4 [...]? ubi Domocritus ubi tu[llius]
5 [... aut] darius Ubi plato ubi pompeius

Canvas 5, 1250,250-2700,2150, 7-11v left block (checked blind by an independent reader, boxes 1200,250-2750,1250 and 1200,1150-2750,2200):
1 [...]phirius? ... Ubi Alexander
2 rex maximus Aristoteles vir doctissimus
3 Ubi cum helena Paris pulcherrimus
4 Achilles ubi magnanimus Ubi Cesar
5 [...] magnus? ubi hector troye fortiss[imus]
6 [...]mus Ubi Salomon sapientissimus

NOT PART OF THE CLAIM: offsets of pages not in the images

Canvas 3 (Stams_STA_Frg_007_05v08v), 2980,392-4011,2308, mirrored and contrast-stretched, offset on 7-8v (Media vita, Cantus 003732; first reading of this area contaminated by the slip):
1 [Medi]a vita in morte sumus que[m]
2 [quaerimus] adiutorem n(isi) te domine
3 [qui pro peccatis] nostris iuste irasce(ris)
4 [Sancte] ... deus
5 [Sancte] ... et misericors sal[vator]
6 amare morti ne tradas

Canvas 5, 4268,343-5299,2063, mirrored, offset on 7-10v (AH str. 7a-b): "[transi]erunt leges mortali[um]", "[spa]cium Sed [tu] deus". The rest is mixed with show-through and was not read.

SLIP ONLY, not seen on any image: "Ubi Sampson robustissimus ubi versucia speciosissimus" ("Absalon" is a conjecture for "versucia" from AH's manuscripts F and G).
